blogs.title: From Text to Tables: How FeatLLM Turns Large Language Models into Feature Engineers
blogs.description: An introductory post that explains the core idea of FeatLLM—using LLMs not for direct predictions but to automatically generate useful features (rules) from raw tabular data. It breaks down what feature engineering is, why it matters for low‑shot learning, and how FeatLLM leverages the reasoning power of LLMs to create human‑readable rules that feed simple downstream models.

blogs.title: Rule‑Based Reasoning Made Easy: The Two‑Step Prompt Design Behind FeatLLM
blogs.description: A deep dive into FeatLLM’s structured prompting strategy. This article walks readers through the three components of the prompt—basic information, reasoning instruction, and response instruction—and shows how the two‑step chain‑of‑thought approach helps the LLM first infer causal relationships and then synthesize concrete decision rules for each class.

blogs.title: Why Simpler Models Win: How FeatLLM Slashes Inference Costs Without Losing Accuracy
blogs.description: Explains how generating rule‑based binary features enables the use of lightweight models like linear regression instead of repeatedly calling an LLM at inference time. The post highlights performance vs. latency trade‑offs, compares inference times across methods, and illustrates why FeatLLM offers near‑state‑of‑the‑art accuracy with far lower computational overhead.

blogs.title: Bagging, Ensembles, and Prompt Size: The Clever Tricks That Keep FeatLLM Scalable
blogs.description: Discusses the practical challenges of limited context windows in large language models and how FeatLLM overcomes them using feature bagging, random sampling of few‑shot examples, and ensemble averaging. The article uses simple analogies to explain why generating multiple rule sets improves robustness and allows FeatLLM to handle tables with hundreds of columns.

blogs.title: FeatLLM vs. Traditional Tabular Learners: A Head‑to‑Head Few‑Shot Benchmark
blogs.description: Presents an accessible summary of the experimental results from 13 diverse datasets. Readers will see side‑by‑side comparisons of AUC scores for FeatLLM against logistic regression, XGBoost, Random Forests, SCARF, STUNT, TabPFN, and other LLM‑based baselines—showing how just 4 shots can rival models trained on 32 examples.

blogs.title: Real‑World Ready: Applying FeatLLM in Healthcare and Finance When Labels Are Scarce
blogs.description: Translates the technical findings into concrete use cases. This post explores how practitioners in domains like medical diagnostics or credit risk assessment can leverage FeatLLM to extract expert‐level rules from limited patient or client data, reducing labeling costs while retaining interpretability.

blogs.title: Ethical Reflections on Trusting LLM Knowledge for Critical Decisions
blogs.description: Offers a balanced discussion on the broader impact of injecting LLM prior knowledge into tabular predictions. Topics include potential biases inherited from training corpora, the risk of over‑reliance on generated rules, and best practices for auditing and validating FeatLLM’s outputs before deployment.
